source_span: We interpret this as effectively signaling a hawkish bias, with the intent of keeping December as a live option for the Committee's next hike. We continue to expect a hike at the December FOMC meeting.
source_chain: JPM: the statement's new 'accumulation of more information' sentence signals a deliberate hawkish bias meant to keep December live, therefore JPM still expects a December hike, therefore the press conference's muddled, data-free rationale for the pause left the market less convinced a December plan exists. No explicit invalidation is given beyond the data remaining supportive; JPM does not name a specific print or threshold that would flip its call.
pulse_chain: Pulse: same two steps (hawkish statement sentence -> JPM still expects December; muddled presser -> market less convinced) are reproduced correctly, but the theme then closes with an invented explicit invalidation: a firm September core PCE print preserves the hawks' December case, a soft one means the market prices 'the first dovish mistake of this chair's tenure.'
why: The closing invalidation is not argued by any cited note - UBS is the only one of the seven that even mentions the core PCE print, and it explicitly says 'the bar to derail a December hike appears high,' i.e. the print is unlikely to swing the outcome, the opposite of the pulse's framing of PCE as a clean binary test that could produce 'the first dovish mistake of this chair's tenure.'
